ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is drawn a circular celestial body labeled “Mars,” with multiple dashed orbits around it, respectively labeled as orbit I, orbit II, and orbit III; among them, orbit I surrounds Mars and is closest to the surface of Mars, with point P also marked beside it, and point Q on the relatively outer orbit. Reasoning: The problem states that orbit I is close to the surface of Mars, so the radius of the spaceship's circular motion on orbit I can be approximately regarded as the radius R of Mars. When the spaceship makes near-surface circular motion around Mars, universal gravitation provides the centripetal force: GMm/R^2 = m·4π^2R/T^2, giving M = 4π^2R^3/(GT^2). The average density of Mars ρ = M/(4/3πR^3); substituting M gives ρ = 3π/(GT^2). It can be seen that after measuring the period T of orbit I, R is eliminated, and the average density of Mars can be inferred. Final conclusion: The density of Mars can be inferred.
